source_evidence.scope: Complete attorney analysis: AI records as ESI, Rule 37(e), prompts and source versions, model and system instructions, human revisions, legal holds, vendor retention, reconstruction limits and proportional preservation.
main_facts: Reuters Legal commentary argues that consequential AI-generated business records may require more than the final document. Prompts, retrieved source versions, model identifiers, system instructions, intermediate outputs, human edits, approvals and triggered actions can determine whether a record is explainable or defensible. The author recommends proportional preservation, updated legal holds and vendor checks rather than retaining every interaction indefinitely.

Classify AI uses by consequence, then preserve the minimum origin package for high-risk records: inputs, versions, outputs, edits, approvals and actions. Test whether vendors can export that package before procurement, because rerunning a prompt cannot reconstruct historical context reliably.

main_facts: GitHub’s tutorial shows how to open a Copilot app session in VS Code while retaining its conversation, code changes and working context. The handoff lets an agent complete broad work remotely before a developer inspects the diff, continues the discussion, edits files and runs local tests. Pushing remains tied to the session’s pull request.

Use session transfer as a review boundary. Confirm the expected branch and worktree, inspect every changed file, rerun project checks and make manual corrections before updating the pull request; preserved context should accelerate review, not substitute for it.

Its Project Perception vision combines signals from identity, data, endpoint, network, cloud and runtime to assess risk before actions, contain behavior and preserve traceability. Turn the control sequence into a read-only review skill: identify the agent and intended task, gather current signals, compare proposed action with permissions, and return allow, contain or escalate. Keep enforcement external and require practitioner judgment for ambiguous risk.
